info.title: Itaja Developers API
info.description:
The Itaja API lets your own systems do what the Itaja dashboard does: create what you sell, register buyers, take payments, and manage what buyers get afterwards — subscriptions, credits, license keys.

## Base URL

| Environment | Base URL |
|---|---|
| Production | `https://api.getitaja.com/api/v1` |
| Development | `https://api-dev.getitaja.com/api/v1` |

## Authentication

Send your API key in the `x-itj-key` header. Keep it on your server: anyone holding it acts as you.

- **Sandbox or live.** A key starting with `itjs_` is a *sandbox* key: nothing is really charged, and it only sees sandbox products. A key starting with `itjp_` is *live*: real money, live products only. The two worlds never mix — a sandbox key cannot read nor touch a live product, a live subscriber or a live wallet.
- **Whole account or one product.** A key can cover your whole account, or be limited to a single product. A product key cannot reach another product (`403 PRODUCT_SCOPE_VIOLATION`).
- A handful of endpoints take **no API key** because they are called from your buyer's device or your shipped software (marked *public* below). They are protected by what the caller holds instead — a license key, or a short-lived signed token your server issued — and they are rate-limited.

## Responses

Every answer has the same shape: `{ "success": true, "data": … }` on success, `{ "success": false, "error": "…", "code": "…" }` on failure. `error` is for humans, `code` is stable and meant for your code. Something that does not exist and something you are not allowed to see answer the same `404`: the API never reveals what belongs to someone else.

## How you sell: the three modes

Every product is sold in exactly one way, chosen when the product is created and never changed afterwards:

| Mode | What the buyer gets | Endpoints you will use |
|---|---|---|
| `SUBSCRIPTION` | Access billed every week, month, quarter or year | **Products**, **Subscriptions** |
| `CREDITS` | A balance of credits (coins) spent as they use your service | **Products**, **Credits**, **Credits (public)** |
| `LICENSE` | A license key that unlocks your software on a number of devices | **Products**, **Licenses**, **Licenses (public)**, **Licenses (retrieval)** |

An endpoint of another mode answers `409 MONETIZATION_MODE_MISMATCH`.

## Which endpoint should I use?

Some endpoints look alike. The difference, in one line each:

- **Selling — Checkout vs. credit pack checkout.** `POST /checkout-sessions` sells a cart *you* price (your line items, your amounts). `POST /products/{productId}/credit-packs/{packId}/checkout` sells a credit bundle priced *by Itaja* (you never send an amount).
- **Credits — wallet vs. balance.** `GET …/credits/{customerId}` returns the balance *and* every movement (for a statement or support). `GET …/credits/{customerId}/balance` returns only the number, and `0` for a buyer who never bought (for showing a counter).
- **Credits — server vs. buyer's device.** `POST …/credits/consume` is called by your server with your API key. `POST /public/credits/consume` is called by the buyer's browser or app with a 15-minute token your server issued (`…/wallet-token`) — your key never leaves your server.
- **Credits — expire one vs. expire all.** `…/credits/expire` clears one buyer's expired credits; `…/credits/expire-due` clears every buyer of the product. Itaja already runs the second every day.
- **Licenses — suspend, revoke, rotate, resend.** *Suspend* blocks a key for a while and can be undone (*resume*). *Revoke* kills it for good. *Rotate* replaces a leaked key with a new one (devices must activate again). *Resend* emails the same key again to a buyer who lost it — nothing changes.
- **Licenses — managing vs. checking.** The **Licenses** endpoints are for you (issue, list, revoke…), with your API key. The **Licenses (public)** endpoints are for the software you ship (verify, activate, deactivate), with the buyer's license key only.
- **Subscriptions — cancel vs. pause.** *Cancel* ends the subscription, at the end of the paid period by default or right away with `immediately: true`. *Pause* freezes it (no renewal, no invoice) until you *resume* it, without losing paid days.
- **There is no "create a subscription" endpoint**, on purpose: a subscription starts when the buyer pays its first period on the product's link.

Categories and endpoints are listed in alphabetical order.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: The catalogue you declare in code — features, subscription plans, credit packs, licences and one-off offers — pushed in one call. Itaja shows you what would change, then makes its catalogue match yours: new versions for changed prices, archived (never deleted) for what you dropped. Called by your server or your deploy pipeline.

tags.name: Checkout
tags.description: Get a payment page for a sale whose content and price **your** system decides — a cart, a quote, a custom amount. You send the line items, Itaja returns a URL to send the buyer to, and tells your server when it is paid. Called by your server.

tags.name: Credits
tags.description: Products sold as credits (coins). Each buyer has **one balance per product**; balances of different products are never added together. Add credits, spend them, read the balance or the full history, sell credit bundles, and issue the short-lived token that lets the buyer's own device use its balance. Called by your server.

tags.name: Credits (public)
tags.description: The same balance, used from the **buyer's browser or app**, without your API key: the caller presents the 15-minute token your server issued. Rate-limited to 60 calls per minute per IP and per token.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: Your buyers. One buyer is one email address. Create, find, update a buyer and read their invoices. Requires a key limited to a product. Called by your server.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Is the API up? No key needed — for your monitoring.

tags.name: Licenses
tags.description: Products sold as license keys. Issue keys (one by one or in bundles for resellers), list them, and manage their life: adjust, suspend, resume, revoke, rotate, resend. Also each product's rules: how long a key lasts and on how many devices. Called by your server.

tags.name: Licenses (public)
tags.description: For the **software you ship**: verify a key, activate it on a device, free a device. No API key — the license key is the proof. Rate-limited to 60 calls per minute per IP and per key. Also the public keys that let your software check a license offline.

tags.name: Licenses (retrieval)
tags.description: Hand a license key to your own website after a purchase without ever putting it in a URL: your success page receives a one-time token, and your server exchanges it for the key. Called by your server.

tags.name: Me
tags.description: Internal: used by the Itaja dashboard to identify the signed-in merchant. Not part of an integration.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: What you sell. A product carries its name, its currency and **its mode** — one-off purchase, subscription, credits or license keys — fixed at creation. Create, list, read, update and archive products. Called by your server.

tags.name: Quotes
tags.description: Know what a sale costs the buyer and what you receive, **before** you create it. You send a price and a currency; Itaja answers the total the buyer pays, your net and the commission, from the fee mode set on your account. Nothing is created and nobody is charged. Called by your server.

tags.name: Subscriptions
tags.description: Your subscribers: who is subscribed to which plan, where each subscription stands, and its invoices. Cancel (at period end or now), pause and resume. Subscriptions are created by the buyer's first payment, never by an API call. Called by your server.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-itj-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Your API key: `itjs_…` for sandbox, `itjp_…` for live. Keep it on your server.

get.description:
**In short:** Check that the API is up. No key needed.

Public health check endpoint

post.description:
**In short:** Create something to sell, and choose once and for all how it is sold: one-off purchase, subscription, credits or license keys.

Creates a product owned by the account behind the API key. The monetization mode is mandatory and immutable.

get.description:
**In short:** List the products this key can see.

Lists the products of the account in the API key's mode (or only the product of a product-scoped API key), newest first. Archived products are excluded unless includeArchived=true.

**In short:** Read one product.

Retrieves a product. Products of another account, or outside the scope of the API key, are reported as not found.

patch.description:
**In short:** Rename a product, change its description or put it on or off sale. How it is sold never changes.

Updates the name, description, metadata, or status of a product. The monetization mode is immutable and is rejected by the schema. A credits product cannot become ACTIVE with an incomplete offer.

metadata.description: Object: shallow one-level merge into the stored metadata (unnamed keys survive, a named key is replaced whole). null: clears metadata. Omitted: untouched.
Object: shallow one-level merge into the stored metadata (unnamed keys survive, a named key is replaced whole). null: clears metadata. Omitted: untouched.
Object: shallow one-level merge into the stored metadata (unnamed keys survive, a named key is replaced whole). null: clears metadata. Omitted: untouched.

post.description:
**In short:** Take a product off sale for good, without deleting its history.

Archives a product (status ARCHIVED + archivedAt). Idempotent: archiving an already archived product returns it unchanged.

get.description:
**In short:** Internal: used by the Itaja dashboard to identify the signed-in merchant. Not meant for integrations.

Returns the authenticated user (validated JWT) and the user profile row (created on first call)

post.description:
**In short:** Register a buyer (name and email) so you can sell to them, credit them or follow their subscriptions.

Creates a new customer for the product associated with the API key. With `merchantCustomerId` — your own user or organisation id — the call is an upsert: the same id with the same email returns the same customer, and every route that takes a `customerId` then accepts your id too. `409 MERCHANT_CUSTOMER_ID_TAKEN` when your id already names another customer of your account; `409 CUSTOMER_ALREADY_MAPPED` when that customer already carries another of your ids.

get.description:
**In short:** Find buyers by email or phone number.

Lists the customers of the product associated with the API key, newest first. `email` and `phone` filter case-insensitively on a substring (both are OR-ed when both are provided).

patch.description:
**In short:** Change a buyer's contact details (name, phone, address).

Updates the contact details of a customer of the product associated with the API key. `merchantCustomerId` names a customer that has none yet; renaming is refused (`409 CUSTOMER_ALREADY_MAPPED`).

get.description:
**In short:** Read one buyer's record.

Retrieves a specific customer by their ID — or by your own `merchantCustomerId` — for the product associated with the API key

**In short:** List the invoices issued to one buyer.

Retrieves all invoices for a specific customer

post.description:
**In short:** Add credits to a buyer's balance: a gift, a compensation, a sale made outside Itaja.

Credits a customer wallet, creating it when needed. Replaying the same idempotencyKey never credits twice. `expiresAt` dates the coins of this grant only (each grant is its own lot; coins already held keep their own expiry, and expired coins are burnt before new ones land); the wallet's `expiresAt` is the earliest expiry among its live coins; `lowBalanceThreshold` is persisted on creation and on an existing wallet.
post.summary: Grant credits to a customer wallet

post.description:
**In short:** Take credits out of a buyer's balance when they use your service. Refused if the balance is too low.

Debits a wallet atomically. Returns 409 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS when the balance is too low.
post.summary: Consume credits from a customer wallet

post.description:
**In short:** Remove the expired credits of one buyer.

Burns exactly the coins of a wallet whose expiry has passed, leaving the coins that are still valid. The operation is idempotent; a later expiry of the same wallet burns again.
post.summary: Expire a due credit wallet balance

post.description:
**In short:** Remove the expired credits of every buyer of a product. Itaja already does this every day.

Sweeps the product wallets holding expired coins and burns those coins only. A daily `credits/expiry-sweep` job does the same across every product.
post.summary: Expire every due wallet of a product

get.description:
**In short:** Read a buyer's balance together with the history of every movement.

Returns the wallet plus its transaction history, newest first.

post.description:
**In short:** Create a short-lived pass (15 minutes) that lets the buyer's browser or app read and spend their own credits, without exposing your API key.

Mints a 15-minute HMAC token that lets the customer read and debit their own wallet through the public routes.

get.description:
**In short:** From the buyer's browser or app: show the balance with the pass issued by your server.

Returns the balance, the low-balance threshold, the expiry and the 5 latest transactions. Public endpoint, limited per IP and per token.
get.summary: Read a wallet with a signed token

post.description:
**In short:** From the buyer's browser or app: spend credits with the pass issued by your server.

Debits the wallet bound to the token. Public endpoint: the token is the only authorization. Limited per IP and per token.
post.summary: Consume credits with a signed token

get.description:
**In short:** Read only the number: how many credits a buyer has left. Zero for a buyer who never bought.

Returns the customer's balance, the product's coin and the currency — without the transaction journal. A customer of the merchant who holds no wallet yet reads `0`; a customer of another merchant, an unknown id, or a product outside the key's scope is a `404`; a product of another monetization mode is a `409 MONETIZATION_MODE_MISMATCH`. The balance is per product: a coin is never summed with another product's.

**In short:** List the credit bundles on sale for a product (for example "100 coins for 1 000 XOF").

Returns the active packs of the product, ordered by position, with the coin's name and the product's credit form. The product is resolved within the API key's scope: an out-of-scope product is a 404, never an empty list; a product of another monetization mode is a 409 MONETIZATION_MODE_MISMATCH.
get.summary: List a product's active credit packs

post.description:
**In short:** Get a payment page for one credit bundle. The price comes from the bundle; you only name the buyer.

Prices the sale from the designated pack (the pack carries the price and the currency — the caller never passes an amount), requires the customer, persists the Itaja checkout with its creditPackId anchoring BEFORE asking the payment provider for the session, and returns the checkout id, the payment URL and the split. A replayed call with the same `reference` returns the same checkout.
post.summary: Start a checkout from a credit pack

post.description:
**In short:** Create one key for one buyer. The key is shown only once: store it or send it.

Generates a new license key for a customer. The clear key is returned exactly once — keep it, everything else uses maskedKey.

get.description:
**In short:** List the keys of a product.

Returns the product license keys, newest first. `data` stays the array; `meta.nextCursor` and `meta.total` paginate it.

**In short:** Read how long this product's keys last and on how many devices they work.

Returns the per-product license duration and default activation limit.

put.description:
**In short:** Choose how long this product's keys last and on how many devices they work.

Sets the product's license duration (lifetime | days-N | from-first-activation-days-N) and its default activation limit (null = unlimited). Other metadata keys are preserved.

get.description:
**In short:** Read one key and the devices it is active on.

Returns a key with its activation history.

patch.description:
**In short:** Change the number of devices or the end date of a key that already exists.

Adjusts activationsMax and/or expiresAt after issuance. Emits a license.updated event carrying the before and after values.

post.description:
**In short:** Cancel a key for good (fraud, refund). It can never work again.

Marks the key REVOKED. A revoked key can never be activated again. An optional reason is kept in the license.revoked event payload.

**In short:** Block a key for a while (an unpaid invoice, a dispute). You can lift it later.

Marks the key SUSPENDED. A suspended key refuses activation; only the creator can lift it with resume.

**In short:** Lift a suspension: the key works again.

Marks a SUSPENDED key ACTIVE again. Only a suspended key can be resumed.

**In short:** Replace a key that leaked: the old one stops working, a new one is issued, and every device must be activated again.

Revokes the key and issues a replacement. The new clear key is returned exactly once; every activated device must re-activate. Use resend instead when the buyer only lost the receipt.

**In short:** Email the same key again to the buyer who lost it. Nothing changes on their devices.

Re-sends the SAME key to the purchase email. No effect on already-activated devices.
post.summary: Resend a license key to its purchaser

post.description:
**In short:** Mark the keys whose validity has ended as expired.

Moves ACTIVE keys past their expiry to EXPIRED.
post.summary: Expire every due license key of a product

get.description:
**In short:** Tells whether this product allows making bundles of keys for resellers.

Returns allowResellerBatches (off unless the creator turns it on). Off means batch creation is refused.

put.description:
**In short:** Allow or forbid bundles of keys for resellers on this product.

Turns batch creation on or off for this product. Other metadata keys (including metadata.license) are preserved.

post.description:
**In short:** Create up to 500 keys at once, to hand to a reseller.

Mints up to 500 keys under one batch and returns them in clear exactly once. Each key keeps its own license.issued event; the batch writes one license.batch_issued. Refused 403 while allowResellerBatches is off, 429 past the account rate limit or quota.
post.summary: Issue a batch of license keys

get.description:
**In short:** List the bundles of keys made for resellers.

Returns the product's batches, newest first, with redemption stats (claimed = at least one activation). Never a clear key.

**In short:** Read one reseller bundle and how many of its keys are in use.

Returns one batch with its redemption stats. Never a clear key.

post.description:
**In short:** Cancel the keys of a reseller bundle that nobody has used yet. Keys in use keep working.

Revokes every still-unclaimed key of the batch and leaves claimed keys untouched (the reseller contract). The batch becomes VOID, terminal. Each revoked key keeps a license.revoked event (reason batch_void).

**In short:** Called by your software to ask "is this key valid, and for my product?". Answers yes or no with the reason.

Returns a verdict (valid: false with a reason) as a normal 200 — an invalid key is an answer, not an error. The verdict names the product (productId, productName, mode) and never the clear key. Send `productId` to bind the check to your product: a key of any other product answers valid: false, reason PRODUCT_MISMATCH. Public endpoint, limited per IP and per key.

**In short:** Called by your software when a buyer enters their key on a device: it takes one of the key's device slots.

Binds the key to an instance, respecting activationsMax. Re-activating the same instance is idempotent; a suspended key is refused (the creator resumes it). With `productId`, a key of another product is refused 422 PRODUCT_MISMATCH before any slot is consumed. Public endpoint, limited per IP and per key.
post.summary: Activate a license key on an instance

post.description:
**In short:** Called by your software to free a device slot, so the buyer can use the key elsewhere.

Releases the activation slot held by an instance. Public endpoint, limited per IP and per key.

**In short:** Your server exchanges the one-time token received after a purchase for the buyer's license key.

Exchanges a single-use token for the clear license key — once. A second attempt is refused (409 LICENSE_RETRIEVAL_ALREADY_REDEEMED); an expired token is refused (410); a token for another account is refused (403). The key is resolved at redemption time, so a rotation between the hand-off and the redemption serves the current key. API key required.

get.description:
**In short:** Tells whether your success page receives a one-time token in place of the license key.

Returns whether the product substitutes a single-use retrieval token for the [license_key] variable of the merchant's success URL. Off by default.
get.summary: Read the [license_key] opt-in of a product

put.description:
**In short:** Turns on or off the one-time token hand-off to your success page.

Enables or disables the [license_key] hand-off for a product. Off by default; other metadata keys are preserved.
put.summary: Set the [license_key] opt-in of a product

post.description:
**In short:** Get a payment page for a sale whose content and price your own system decides (a cart, a quote). Send the line items, receive a URL to send the buyer to.

Prices the sale from the caller's line items (subtotal, platform fee from the merchant's feeMode, total) in integer minor units, persists the Itaja checkout BEFORE asking the payment provider for the session, and returns the checkout id, the payment URL and the split. A retried call with the same `reference` returns the same checkout and session.
post.summary: Create a checkout for a dynamic sale

post.description:
**In short:** Ask what a sale will cost the buyer and what you will receive, before you create anything. Send a price and a currency; nothing is created and nobody is charged.

Returns what the payer would be charged (`total`), what the merchant would receive (`merchantNet`) and the commission broken down (`fees`), from the merchant's fee mode. Nothing is created and the payment engine is not called. The same figures a checkout of that price would carry.

**In short:** One call moves a customer to a plan of a subscription product — new subscription, upgrade, downgrade, cancel to the free plan, or undo a pending change.

`customerId` is Itaja's id or your own. `outcome` says what happened:

- `payment_required` — no subscription yet, paid plan: send the customer to `paymentUrl` (bound to this customer, it returns to your `successUrl` / `cancelUrl`). The URL expires at `paymentUrlExpiresAt` (24 h): past it the pay page answers `410`, call `subscribe` again. Nothing is created until the first period is paid.
- `on_default_plan` — no subscription, the product's default (free) plan: nothing is written, the customer is on it.
- `upgrade_pending` — a higher plan: the prorated difference is invoiced now and payable at `paymentUrl`; the new plan applies once it is paid.
- `change_scheduled` — a lower plan (or any change during a free trial): applied at `scheduledChange.effectiveAt`, the next period is billed at the new price.
- `cancel_scheduled` — the default plan: the subscription ends at the end of the paid period.
- `pending_cleared` — the current plan while a change or a cancel was pending: both are undone and the next period is billed again.
- `unchanged` — nothing to do; a replay of the same call lands here.

`404 PLAN_NOT_FOUND` / `CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND` outside the key's reach. `409 PLAN_CHANGE_NOT_SUPPORTED` across currencies or billing intervals, `409 INVALID_CONTRACT_TRANSITION` on a paused subscription, `409 CONTRACT_HELD_BY_PROVIDER` on a card-billed one.
post.summary: Subscribe a customer to a plan

get.description:
**In short:** See who is subscribed to what, and where each subscription stands. Filter by product, plan, buyer or status.

One row per subscription, newest first, with its customer, plan and product. Optional filters: `productId`, `planId`, `customerId`, `status` (`TRIALING`, `ACTIVE`, `PAUSED`, `CANCELED`, `ENDED`; anything else is `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`). A key only sees the subscriptions of its own mode (sandbox or live) and, when scoped to a product, of that product — asking for another product is `403 PRODUCT_SCOPE_VIOLATION`.

**In short:** Read one subscription and the invoices of its periods.

`404 SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown id and for a subscription outside the key's reach (another account, another product, another mode) alike.
get.summary: Retrieve a subscription and its invoices

post.description:
**In short:** Stop a subscription, at the end of the period already paid (default) or right away.

`immediately: false` (default) keeps the subscription until the end of the paid period and voids any invoice already issued for a later period; `immediately: true` ends it now, without refund, and voids every unpaid invoice. Paid invoices are never touched. `409 INVALID_CONTRACT_TRANSITION` on a subscription already ended, `409 CONTRACT_HELD_BY_PROVIDER` on a card-billed (`AUTOMATIC`) subscription.

**In short:** Freeze a subscription: no renewal and no invoice while it is paused.

`ACTIVE → PAUSED`: no renewal while paused. `409 CANNOT_PAUSE_TRIAL` during a free trial, `409 INVALID_CONTRACT_TRANSITION` from any other status, `409 CONTRACT_HELD_BY_PROVIDER` on a card-billed (`AUTOMATIC`) subscription.

**In short:** Restart a paused subscription. The days already paid are not lost.

`PAUSED → ACTIVE`. The pause is added to the current period, so no paid day is lost. `409 INVALID_CONTRACT_TRANSITION` if the subscription is not paused, `409 CONTRACT_HELD_BY_PROVIDER` on a card-billed (`AUTOMATIC`) subscription.

put.description:
**In short:** Send the whole catalogue you declare in code — features, subscription plans, credit packs and licences — and Itaja makes its own match it. Add `?dryRun=true` to see what would change without changing anything.

Each item is named by **your** `id`. Items that are new are `created`; items that differ are `changed`; items you no longer declare are `archived` (taken off sale, never deleted — running contracts keep going); the rest is `unchanged`. Pushing the same catalogue twice changes nothing the second time.

Changing a plan's price, currency, interval or included features creates a **new version** of the plan: new subscriptions take it, existing subscriptions stay on the version they bought. Name, description, trial and `default` change in place.

The catalogue is the one of the key's mode: a sandbox key pushes the sandbox catalogue, a live key the live one. Products you created in the dashboard, or with `POST /products`, are never changed or archived by a push.
